title: Red's small group and the 1936 recordings
summary: Personnel of Red's small group, drums or no drums, Polly Wolly Doodle and Gramercy Square, and his mellophone.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x:
After that Red started this
small group with Dave Barbour and Stuie
Pletcher and Herbie Haymer, Pete Peterson.
when there was no drums; correct? It was kind of famous for that reason, as I recall.
It might have been. I always remember Maurice being there.
Yes; the first one had drums. Let's see, here's January '36 [Stew Fletcher] with Stew Fletcher, Donald McCork, Herbie Haymer, you, Dave Barbour, Pete Peterson, Bob White on drums, and Red.
That's when you did "Polly Wolly Doodle".
I don't know why I wrote myself in on the mellophone; that's probably what it was.
Because of the bad lip, you mean?
It did, and also it didn't require one to be as precise in intonation I guess. You really didn't have to be a good player.
